op_constraints: op-subset (ops_supported.json): FFT stages cannot slice/index-register values; partner/group values are fetched via address-computed GM loads inside one kernel (in-kernel scratch ping-pong). Constraints: supported = load/store(addr-arithmetic gather), where(same shape), //, %, cos/sin, full sum; unsupported = slice, reg/scalar index, trans, sum(axis), join/split/cat, chained None, python math in jit; reshape passes the frontend but crashes the XPU lowering (GlobalEncodingAttr UNREACHABLE) -> no kernel here uses reshape.  NOTE (stale-read bug): the GM ping-pong pattern is unreliable: store->permuted-load from the same buffer returns stale values at grid>1 (this WP) and — per WP3's size sweep — also at grid=1 for n=32/64; see wp2_concurrency.json and wp3_blockmax.json.  The scalar codegen kernel sidesteps the whole op-subset: unrolling happens in python, the jit body is pure scalar load/compute/store.

fused.ownership: one program owns all 4 stages of the packet
fused.local_live_data_range: register v across 4 stages + scratch ping-pong
fused.synchronization_scope: program-order only; no cross-launch visibility needed

expected_gm_bytes.formula: gm_rad2(N,L): stage0 v+partner loads, per-stage partner load + result store, final output store

split_2kernel.ownership: kernel A owns stages 0..h-1 + handoff buffer; kernel B owns stages h..3 from handoff to output
split_2kernel.local_live_data_range: register v per kernel; GM handoff RE/IM (2x2x16B)
split_2kernel.synchronization_scope: launch-order (host stream) establishes handoff visibility via gm_launch_order_visibility=PASS (WP1)

expected_gm_bytes.formula: gm_rad2(N,L) + 2*N*4 (kernel B re-loads its own vector from the handoff: register state cannot cross kernel boundaries)

delta.interpretation: fusion saves one host launch plus one full vector reload (split kernel B re-materializes its register state from the handoff buffer); N=16 is launch-dominated so latency ordering is reported as measured, not interpreted
